header: DEV-ONLY protection against "EntityMetadataNotFoundError: No metadata for "Circular" was found". What happens: in `next dev` a route file is compiled the FIRST time it is used, and it then gets its OWN fresh copy of the entity classes (Circular, User, ...). TypeORM finds an entity's metadata by the class OBJECT (a Map keyed by the class), not by its name, so the new copy is a stranger to the connection that was created with the old copy -- even though they are identical -- and the first request fails. The next request works, because the connection has been rebuilt by then. That is the "error on the first open of a new circular, clean the second time" you saw. My fix: in development only, when TypeORM does not know a class OBJECT, I accept the registered entity with the SAME NAME. Production has no hot reload and one copy of each class, so nothing changes there.

symbols.name: hasExactMetadata
symbols.sig: export function hasExactMetadata(ds: DataSource, entity: unknown): boolean
doc: Returns true only if the connection was built with this very class object, not merely one with the same name.

symbols.name: classNameOf
doc: Returns the name of a class (a function with a name), else undefined.

behaviours: the two copies really are different objects with the same name
BEFORE the fix: a reloaded copy of the class fails exactly like the log (EntityMetadataNotFoundError, No metadata for "Circular")
BEFORE the fix: the strict check and TypeORM's own hasMetadata agree the copy is unknown
AFTER the fix: find() through the reloaded copy returns the rows
AFTER the fix: create() + save() work and write to the real table
AFTER the fix: the metadata found is the registered Circular
the strict check still says the copy is NOT the registered class (a real reload stays detectable)
...while hasMetadata() now says yes for the copy (which is why the strict check exists)
a class with a different name is still rejected
a string target and the registered class itself behave as before
